newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-MOORER STOPS BOTHA IN BRUISING BATTLE.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-MOORER STOPS BOTHA IN BRUISING BATTLE.

text.p: Michael Moorer kept his International Boxing Federation (IBF) heavyweight title Saturday by pounding out a bruising win over Francois Botha that was stopped early in the final round.
Referee Mills Lane stepped in to wave off the beating with Botha in trouble against the ropes just 18 seconds into the 12th round.
"The way he was talking before the fight I knew he would be tough and it was a tough fight," Moorer said. "If I was taking those shots, I probably got a broken jaw."

Moorer, who improved to 38-1, battered the South African's face, nearly closing the left eye with a steady barrage of punishing right jabs and powerful lefts and put the game challenger on the floor twice in the 11th round.
The second knockdown came just before the bell and somehow Botha got up and stumbled his way across the ring to get to his stool and continue for a few more seconds.
"I fought my heart out," said Botha, 36-1.

Trainer Teddy Atlas was in Moorer's corner, though he had faced the possibility of being suspended 24 hours earlier by the Nevada Athletic Commission for his part in a weigh-in fracas with a reporter Friday.
Moorer and Botha were the featured undercard attraction on the Mike Tyson-Evander Holyfield World Boxing Association championship bout that followed.

In an another heavyweight bout on the undercard for a sellout crowd of 16,000 jammed into the MGM Grand, Briton Henry Akinwande punished Alexander Zolkin with a barrage of lethal right hands to retain his World Boxing Organisation title when the fight was stopped in the 10th round.
"The guy was strong, I hit him with some good shots," Akinwande said.

Akinwande, 40-0-1, put Zolkin, 24-3, down in the fourth round and turned the Russian challenger's face into a bloody pulp before the fight was stopped by ringside physician Dr. Flip Homansky at 2:32 of the 10th round due to a deep cut above the right eye.
"I felt I could continue, I could see, but the doctor didn't think so," said Zolkin.
Said Homansky: "He was squinting and couldn't see."
Mexican Ricardo Lopez made his 17th successful defence of his World Boxing Council strawweight title by stopping Morgan Nduma at 55 seconds of the fifth round.
Lopez, 43-0, had pounded the South African challenger, nearly closing both of his eyes before referee Jay Nady stopped the bout.
Earlier, Antonio Cermeno of Venezuela retained his World Boxing Association junior featherweight title by stopping Eddie Saenz of Nicaragua, who failed to answer the bell for the sixth round.
